_meta: coverage-strategist proposal 2026-11-14 for future-of-software-engineers (AI Engineering Simplified, VERY SIMPLE build). Timecodes = FINAL spine seconds (spine/ALL.e.enhanced.mp4, 477.38 s), cued off ALL.e.enhanced.medium-words.json. Gated face, 9 FACE windows, no title cards (one bed), no clip inserts, no whiteboard beats, no Envato, no ChatGPT images, no captions. Cover layer = 6 receipts (C5 C6 C7 C12 C9 C10), 2 system-design diagrams (C1 C2), 2 animated charts (C3 C4), 17 deck cards (D1 to D13, D15 to D18; D14 folded into C4's takeaway line). On-screen text follows AS-RECORDED's mishear list (Claude, AAARRR, codebase, forward-deployed, workflow automation) and its fact-framing traps.

cover_beats.spoken: Start with Google. In October of 2024, their CEO said that more than a quarter of all new code was generated by AI. By the fall of 2025, it was 50%. By April, 2026, 75. Anthropic moved even faster. Before Claude Code launched in February of 2025, Claude's share of their code was in the low single digits. By May of 2026, Claude had authored more than 80% of the code they merged. By September, over 90%. Both companies describe the same change.

cover_beats.spoken: Here's how software has usually been built. Engineers work in a pod inside their company. A small cross-functional team, typically of 10 people or fewer, working on one or more steps of a funnel or features of a product. A typical pod looked like this, a front engineer, a backend engineer, a QA engineer, a project manager, a designer, maybe a marketer, six seats, six people.
